_about: Hot Takes: the fourth AI-authored lane (owner-approved 2026-11-12, "New AI lane"). Columnist opinions per completed season, written only by a takes.set upload mutation; every figure cited in stats[] with its source and checked like the Season Story (scripts/story_check.py check_takes). Never hand-edit.

Y90.trigger: Audit stale-number warnings for the Y90 takes after the Y92 update
Y90.intro: The Y90 season is in the books, and the numbers have opinions. Every figure below comes straight from the league data. The arguments are ours to defend.

takes.headline: The Falcons Dynasty Belonged to Dorren Skura, and Ryland Maxwell's Numbers Prove It
takes.dek: Three seasons in Atlanta with Skura, three without him: the same back, two different careers.
body: From Y85 through Y87, with Skura on the Atlanta sideline, Ryland "Mad Max" Maxwell ran for 2,617, 2,150 and 2,669 yards. The Falcons won the title all three years. Then Skura left for Philadelphia. Maxwell stayed, and his next three seasons came in at 1,403, 1,172 and 1,223 yards.

Shorter seasons explain only part of it. Without the long playoff runs, Maxwell played 17 games in each of the last two years after 20 in Y87. Per game he fell from 133 rushing yards in Y87 to 72 in Y90. The Falcons fell with him, to 9-8, while Skura won two more titles in Philadelphia. Systems travel. Running backs, it turns out, do not.

stats.label: Maxwell rushing yards per game, Y87
Maxwell rushing yards per game, Y90

takes.headline: Game for Game, Bones Crawford Is Already Out-Throwing Sherman Brandson
takes.dek: The record holder owns the totals. The Eagles quarterback owns the rates, everything except the interceptions.
body: Sherman Brandson's 91,463 passing yards and 1,150 touchdown passes are not going anywhere. Measure the two quarterbacks by the game, though, and the order flips. Bones Crawford has thrown for 297 yards per game to Brandson's 290. He has two MVP awards and two rings in his first 59 games.

The case against him is real, and it is one number: 1.29 interceptions per game, double Brandson's 0.63. The Doctor does not need to throw more. He needs to throw fewer to the other team. Fix that, and this stops being a hot take.

takes.headline: Philadelphia Was the Better Team in Y90; Houston Was the Luckier One
takes.dek: The Eagles allowed fewer points and won by more. The Texans won every close game they played.
body: Houston's 16-1 season is real, and so is the 32-22 win in Super Bowl CXLIX. But the Eagles allowed 360 points to Houston's 381 and finished with a point differential of 203 to Houston's 196. On points scored and allowed, the Texans project to about 12.4 wins. They won 16, and they went 5-0 in one-score games.
Close games are where luck lives, and luck does not carry over from one season to the next. Philadelphia's margins are the better bet to last into Y91.

stats.label: Texans expected wins (points for and against)

takes.headline: Houston Won a Title Without a Single S-Grade Card, and the League Should Copy It
takes.dek: The champions' best-graded player is an A. The balance around him did the rest.
body: Siran Spector is the best-graded Texan on the market, at A. Tim Sweeney grades C and Preston Gore B. No one on the roster carries an S, and Houston went 16-1 anyway.

Look at how it happened. Sweeney threw 36 touchdown passes against 4 interceptions. Spector ran for 29 touchdowns. The defense allowed 381 points, second only to Philadelphia. Nobody had to be the best player in the league because nobody gave the game away. Every front office chasing one superstar card should study the club that won without one.

takes.headline: Lane McCoy's Touchdown Total Is a Compiler's Number, Not a Legend's
takes.dek: Two other backs built nearly the same career, and the three of them share one ring.
body: Lane McCoy has 21,940 rushing yards and 409 rushing touchdowns, more touchdowns than any running back in the league. It sounds like greatness until the neighbors show up. Danny Diggs finished with 21,421 yards and 408 touchdowns. Trequan Jensen finished with 21,690 yards and 388.

Same volume, same shape, and between the three of them, one Super Bowl ring, Jensen's with Green Bay in Y79. McCoy's Broncos went 3-14 this season. Longevity is a skill, and McCoy has plenty of it. It is not the same thing as being the best.

takes.headline: Lamar Jackson Is the Most Overrated Legend in the League
takes.dek: The rushing yards are historic. The touchdown production is not.
body: No quarterback has run like Lamar Jackson. His 7,939 rushing yards are more than three times the 2,396 of Jayden Daniels, the next quarterback on the list. That is the highlight reel, and it is why the reputation is so big.

Count his touchdowns, passing and rushing together, and Jackson produced 2.25 per game over 345 games. Sherman Brandson threw 3.65 touchdown passes per game before a single run is added. Dennis Baylon totaled 3.40 per game and Ray Waller 2.84. Jackson has 2 rings and no Super Bowl MVP. The runs were real. The scoreboard puts him a tier below.

takes.headline: Releasing Kenyon Shaheed Was the Right Call
takes.dek: Philadelphia let its tight end go with his card at its peak, right after his quietest season.
body: Philadelphia released Kenyon Shaheed after Y90, and the timing was right. His card had never looked better: his rating jumped from 69 to 85 over the season. The production went the other way. He caught 56 passes for 782 yards in Y90, down from 74 catches and 1,141 yards in Y89.

This passing game runs through its receivers. Kaulani Rahman gained 2,495 yards and Calvin Wingo II 2,218, each well over twice what Shaheed gave the Eagles. A tight end priced on an 85 rating was a luxury this offense did not need.

takes.headline: God Johnson, Not Sherman Brandson, Is the Most Dominant Player the League Has Seen
takes.dek: Brandson leads the next quarterback by a sliver. Johnson leads the next receiver by a mile.
body: Brandson's 91,463 passing yards lead Wayne Wilson's 90,450 by 1,013, and Wilson needed 431 games to get there. God Johnson's 36,005 receiving yards lead Ian Finney's 32,980 by 3,025, at a position that gains far fewer yards to begin with. In touchdowns it is 378 for Johnson and 292 for Finney, a gap of 86, and Johnson did it in 234 games to Finney's 250.
He also holds the receiving season record on the board, 4,247 yards in Y62. Brandson is the greatest quarterback. Johnson is further ahead of everyone else.

takes.headline: Ray Waller's Interceptions Should Keep Him Out of the Greatest-Quarterback Debate
takes.dek: Nobody has thrown more of them, and every passer with more career yards protects the ball better.
body: Ray Waller has 70,128 passing yards, 749 touchdown passes and 5 rings. He also has 214 interceptions, the most of any quarterback in the league and 2 more than Wayne Wilson, who needed 431 games to Waller's 278.

His ratio of touchdowns to interceptions is 3.5. Sherman Brandson's is 5.81 and Jason Macleone's 6.02. Every quarterback with more career passing yards than Waller has a better ratio. The comebacks made the nickname. The turnovers made them necessary.

takes.headline: Dennis Baylon's 7,452-Yard Season Will Never Be Broken
takes.dek: Not by Brandson, and not by the best young passer Skura has had in years.
body: Dennis Baylon threw for 7,452 yards for Skura's Bills in Y33, and the record board has not moved since. Not even Sherman Brandson, whose 94 touchdown passes in Y55 sit on the same board, got past it.

Bones Crawford is the best young passer Skura has had in years. He opened his career with 5,922 yards in Y88 and still finished 1,530 short. His Y90 brought 5,327. The game has changed around the record, and nobody is getting there.

Y91.intro: Y91 crowned the Eagles again, sent four new names into the Hall and pushed one out. The arguments below are ours to defend; every figure comes straight from the league data.

takes.headline: Bones Crawford Won MVP in the Weakest Season of His Career
takes.dek: Fewest yards, fewest touchdowns, two missed games, and a trophy anyway. His receivers carried the load.
body: The Doctor threw for 5,010 yards and 59 touchdowns in Y91. Those are the lowest totals of his four seasons, well down from 6,302 yards and 72 touchdowns in Y89. Injury cost him 2 of the Eagles' 20 games. He won the MVP anyway.

Follow the yards. Calvin Wingo II caught 2,570 of them with 30 touchdowns and took the Super Bowl MVP. Kaulani Rahman added 1,893 more. The one real step forward belongs to Crawford himself: 18 interceptions, his fewest yet, after 23 in Y90. Credit him for listening. But an MVP for the weakest year of a quarterback's career is an award for the team's record, and Wingo had the better claim to it.

takes.headline: Trae Corral's One Season Is Already Worth More Than Tajae Westry's Whole Career
takes.dek: Career Legacy has the rookie ahead of a quarterback who played 354 games. For once, the number is right.
body: Tajae Westry retired with 60,882 passing yards and 594 touchdown passes across 354 games, every one of them, as far as the books show, for the Raiders. He retired without a ring or an MVP award, and without ever taking the franchise to a Super Bowl.

His successor needed one year. Trae Corral sits at a Career Legacy of 6,180 after 21 games; Westry finished at 6,081. Corral won Rookie of the Year and took the Raiders to Super Bowl CL, the first Super Bowl trip in club history. They lost it 38-23 to Philadelphia, and it still beats anything the previous regime produced. Volume is not greatness. Westry is the proof, and Corral is the correction.

stats.label: Corral Career Legacy after one season

takes.headline: Quenton Fuller and Keion Orzech Had the Same Career. Only One Is a Hall of Famer.
takes.dek: Fuller rose into the Hall by playing Y91. Orzech fell out of it without playing at all.
body: Line them up. Fuller: 280 games, 1,355 tackles, 15 sacks, no rings. Orzech: 271 games, 1,296 tackles, 13 sacks, no rings. Two durable defensive linemen who never won anything, separated by about one season of work.

Fuller's Career Legacy climbed to 7,669 this year and carried him into the Hall. Orzech has not played since Y88. He slid 36 points to 7,283 anyway and dropped below the floor that keeps earlier inductees in. A Hall of Fame that can expel a retired player because the league moved around him is not measuring careers. It is measuring the weather. Either both of these men belong, or neither does.

takes.headline: Akiem Brock Is Already the Best Offensive Lineman the League Has Ever Seen
takes.dek: More blocks per game than any lineman in the books, and a Y91 that more than doubled the next-best season.
body: Hall of Famers Calais Ham, Jakeem Friend and Jawill Perkins averaged between 2.0 and 2.2 blocks a game over their careers. Akiem Brock is at 2.9 after 80 games, and Y91 made even that look modest: 68 blocks in 20 games. The next-best lineman in the league, Cordale Sweezy, had 32.

Brock went into the Hall this year with 3 rings in four seasons. Linemen do not win MVP awards, and he will not need one. When the best protector the league has produced is the one keeping The Doctor upright, the passing totals in Philadelphia start to explain themselves.

takes.headline: Ryland Maxwell Was Never Washed. He Just Needed Dorren Skura Again.
takes.dek: Back in Skura's backfield, Mad Max ran like his old self again, and he did it in 16 games.
body: By Y90, Ryland "Mad Max" Maxwell was averaging 72 rushing yards a game in Atlanta, and it looked like the end. One trade later, back under Skura in Philadelphia, he ran for 1,778 yards and 25 touchdowns at 111 yards a game and won Offensive Player of the Year.
He did it in 16 games. The Eagles played 20, and injury cost him the other 4. The decline was never in his legs. It was in the system around him, and that system has a name.
The trade had no loser, either. Gerrit Ogbah ran for 1,477 yards and 30 touchdowns in Atlanta, and the Falcons went 11-6. The only people who lost were the ones who called Maxwell finished.

takes.headline: Trae Corral Is Not the Next Doctor. He Is the Anti-Doctor, and That Is Better.
takes.dek: One interception in 21 rookie games. No quarterback in the books has protected the ball like that.
body: The comparison writes itself and gets it backwards. Bones Crawford throws for 293 yards a game and has thrown 94 interceptions in 77 games. Trae Corral threw for 4,234 yards and 33 touchdowns over 21 games, about 202 a game, with 1 interception all season. That is the lowest interception rate of any quarterback in the league's books.

Corral's completions went for far fewer yards than Crawford's. He does not beat teams over the top. He refuses to lose to them, and that took an 11-6 Raiders team with 9.8 expected wins all the way to the Super Bowl. Crawford's game needs the best roster in football. Corral's travels anywhere.

takes.headline: The Y91 Eagles Were No Better Than the Y90 Team That Lost. February Was Just Kinder.
takes.dek: Nearly identical point differentials and expected wins. One Super Bowl simply went the other way.
body: Philadelphia outscored opponents by 203 points in Y90 and by 222 in Y91. Expected wins put the two teams at 12.6 and 12.7. That is the same team. The gap in the standings was luck: the Y91 Eagles won 15 games, 2.3 more than their scoring said they should, and went 4-1 in one-score games.

This is a defense of the Y90 club, not a knock on Skura. Losing Super Bowl CXLIX 32-22 to Houston was not a failure of construction. It was one bad night against a team riding its own luck. The Y91 Eagles even lost at home to the 4-13 Bears, the upset of the season. Great teams lose those and win the title anyway, which is all Y91 really added.

takes.headline: Houston's Title Season Was a Mirage, and the Y91 Hangover Proved It
takes.dek: From first in the power rankings to 26th in one year. The coin flips stopped landing.
body: Last year this column called Houston the luckier team. Y91 settled the argument. The Texans went 16-1 in Y90 on scoring that projected 12.4 wins, 3.6 short of what they collected, and they won all 5 of their one-score games on the way to the title.

Then the bounces evened out. Houston went 6-11 in Y91, was outscored by 80 points, finished 26th in the power rankings and lost its last five games. Champions regress; that is normal. Falling from first to 26th is not regression. It is the bill arriving for a season that was never as good as its record.

takes.headline: Terron Stidham Was a Hall of Famer Long Before the Numbers Admitted It
takes.dek: Second in career tackles, and he crossed the bar in a season he never played.
body: Terron Stidham retired with 3,132 tackles, 53 behind K'Lavon Settle for the most in league history, plus 34 interceptions over 282 games. When he finished his last season in Y90, his Career Legacy stood at 7,470, short of the bar. He did not play a down in Y91. His Legacy rose 52 points to 7,522 anyway, and in he went.

Nothing about Stidham changed. The league around him did, the same drift that pushed Keion Orzech out this year. The induction is right. The timing is absurd. A defensive back with the second-biggest tackle total ever should not need a year of retirement and a recalculation to get through the door.

takes.headline: Lane McCoy Will Break the Rushing Record With Three Times the Fumbles of the Man He Passes
takes.dek: Ninety yards from Rondale Ikarras, and more fumbles than any running back the league has recorded.
body: Lane McCoy needs 90 yards to pass Rondale Ikarras. Credit the durability: 307 games and 23,088 yards. Then read the other column. McCoy has fumbled more than any running back in the books, about three times as often as Ikarras, who fumbled 83 times on his way to 23,178 yards, won 9 rings and was Super Bowl MVP 5 times. McCoy has no rings and no awards.

Per game, they are the same back: McCoy averages 75 yards, Ikarras averaged 76. Same production, triple the giveaways, none of the hardware. And the record may not stay with him long. Ryland Maxwell sits 2,371 yards behind McCoy with a career average of 92 a game. McCoy is about to take the record. Maxwell is built to take it from him.

takes.headline: Minnesota's 13-4 Was Built on Coin Flips. San Francisco's 4-12-1 Was Built on Bad Ones.
takes.dek: One-score games pulled the two clubs further apart than their scoring ever did.
body: The Vikings went 7-1 in one-score games and finished 13-4, second in the power rankings. Their scoring said 10.1 wins. That 2.9-win gap was the biggest stroke of luck in the league. The 49ers went 2-10-1 in one-score games and finished 4-12-1 with the scoring of a 7.6-win team, 3.1 wins worse than they played, the unluckiest season anywhere.

Bet on both reversing in Y92. Minnesota's point differential of 90 trailed Carolina's 98 and the Rams' 101, and both of those clubs also went 13-4. San Francisco was outscored by 49, which is bad, but not that bad.

Y92.intro: Y92 gave Philadelphia another title and the league a new career rushing leader. Neither settles as much as it seems. The arguments below are ours to defend; every figure comes straight from the league data.

takes.headline: Lane McCoy's Rushing Record Is a One-Year Lease. Ryland Maxwell Is 951 Yards Away.
takes.dek: McCoy took the record by outlasting everyone. Maxwell is running at a pace neither McCoy nor Rondale Ikarras ever touched.
body: Lane McCoy finished Y92 with 24,507 career rushing yards and passed the 23,178 Rondale Ikarras left behind. Enjoy the banner in Denver while it hangs. McCoy needed 326 games to get there, an average of 75.2 yards a game, a shade under the 76.5 Ikarras managed. That is not a better back taking a record. That is a comparable back playing 23 more games.

The real threat passed Ikarras this year too. Ryland Maxwell sits at 23,556 after only 245 games, 96.1 yards a game, and he ran for 2,839 in Y92 alone. He is 951 short. Run that season again and the record changes hands next year, this time to a back with 9 rings. McCoy has none.

takes.headline: A Cardinals Rookie Outran Lane McCoy in the Year McCoy Broke the Record
takes.dek: Roderic Trawick matched McCoy's touchdowns and beat his yardage in fewer games, for a team that won five.
body: Roderic Trawick ran for 1,455 yards and 29 touchdowns in his first season, in 17 games for a Cardinals team that went 5-12. Lane McCoy, in his record season, ran for 1,419 yards and 29 touchdowns in 19 games for an 11-6 Broncos club. The rookie gained 85.6 yards a game; the record holder gained 74.7.

Nobody is building Trawick a statue after one year. But McCoy's season will be remembered for the number it reached, not for what it was: an ordinary year from a back who has made a career of ordinary years, stacked higher than anyone else's. A rookie on a last-place team showed what a great rushing season looks like.

stats.label: McCoy rushing yards per game, Y92

takes.headline: Bones Crawford Was Robbed: He Matched the MVP's Touchdown Passes in Five Fewer Games
takes.dek: Korey Friend threw 49 touchdown passes in 21 games. Crawford threw 49 in 16, after injury cost him 4.
body: A year ago this column said Bones Crawford won an MVP he did not deserve. This year he deserved the one he did not win. Injury cost The Doctor 4 of the Eagles' 20 games, and he still threw 49 touchdown passes, the same number as Korey Friend, who played 21 games for the Colts. That is 3.06 touchdown passes a game against Friend's 2.33.

Friend's case is his 4 interceptions against Crawford's 17, and it is a real case. But Crawford ran the league's best offense, one that scored 652 points in the regular season, and the Eagles went 15-2. Friend's Colts met them in Super Bowl CLI and lost 30-21. The most valuable player in Y92 was the one whose team nobody could stop.

takes.headline: Philadelphia Traded the Defensive Player of the Year Before He Won It, and Was Right To
takes.dek: Dwayne Skura piled up 233 tackles in Indianapolis. The Eagles allowed fewer points without him, then beat him in the Super Bowl.
body: Dwayne Skura made 124 tackles for the Eagles in Y91. Traded to the Colts, he made 233 with 5 interceptions in Y92 and won Defensive Player of the Year. On paper that is a disaster for Philadelphia. On the field it was nothing of the sort.

The Eagles allowed 373 points in the regular season, down from 384 with Skura in the lineup, and were the league's best defense for a second straight year. The Colts allowed 471. Tackle totals pile up on defenses that spend a lot of time on the field, and Indianapolis did. Then came Super Bowl CLI: Eagles 30, Colts 21. Skura lost the title game to the club that let him go. Moving a player a year early is how dynasties stay dynasties.

takes.headline: The Kaulani Rahman Trade Was a Heist, and a Rookie Is the Reason
takes.dek: Rahman's production collapsed in Los Angeles. Keenan Viennes nearly matched his old numbers in Philadelphia.
body: Kaulani Rahman caught 102 passes for 1,893 yards for the Eagles in Y91. With the Rams in Y92 he caught 57 for 637. It is not only volume: his yards per catch fell from 18.6 to 11.2, and the Rams finished 9-8.

Meanwhile Keenan Viennes, a rookie, caught 91 passes for 1,756 yards and 19 touchdowns in Philadelphia and graded S on the card. Calvin Wingo II added 1,764 yards and the Offensive Player of the Year award. Philadelphia sold a receiver with a big name and replaced him from within at almost no cost in production. Los Angeles bought the name.

takes.headline: Teven Charles Won Rookie of the Year With 552 Yards. Keenan Viennes Had 1,756.
takes.dek: The offensive rookie award went to the least productive candidate in the class. Three first-year players had a stronger case.
body: Teven Charles caught 62 passes for 552 yards and 8 touchdowns for the Panthers. That is 29.1 yards a game, and it earned a C-minus grade and the Rookie of the Year award. Keenan Viennes caught 91 for 1,756 and 19 touchdowns for the champions, with an S grade. Roderic Trawick ran for 1,455 yards and 29 touchdowns. Sione Garland threw 40 touchdown passes against 1 interception.

Charles's Panthers won the NFC South at 12-5, and that looks like the whole argument. A rookie award that rewards the team around a player is a standings table with a name on it. Viennes was the best first-year player in the league. Charles was a passenger.

takes.headline: Sione Garland Is the Best Rookie Quarterback in the Class. Ignore His Career Legacy Anyway.
takes.dek: Garland's 6,718 looks historic. Trae Corral's rookie number lost 2,824 points in one year.
body: Sione Garland threw 40 touchdown passes and 1 interception in 19 games for the Broncos. Ja'Marr Chark, the class's other rookie quarterback, threw 25 and 4 in 17 games for the Buccaneers and graded D-minus. Garland is the better quarterback, and it is not close.

Now the warning. Garland's Career Legacy already reads 6,718 after one season. Trae Corral's read 6,180 after his. A year later Corral sits at 3,356, down 2,824, after a perfectly respectable 3,159 yards and 26 touchdown passes. The rookie number is a projection, and projections get corrected. Judge Garland in Y94.

takes.headline: Two Men Walked Back Into the Hall of Fame This Year Without Playing a Down
takes.dek: Kyric McQuay and Keion Orzech rose on league drift. Kyron Atwell earned his way in with 230 tackles.
body: Kyric McQuay's Career Legacy rose from 7,459 to 7,531 in Y92, over the bar, and he is back in the Hall. His career line did not move: 313 games before the season, 313 after. Keion Orzech last played in Y88. He entered at 7,526 that year, slid out of the Hall at 7,283 in Y91 and drifted back to 7,364 this year. Neither man did a thing.

Compare Kyron Atwell, who made 230 tackles in Y92 and added 643 points to reach 7,780. That is what a Hall of Fame entry should look like. Meanwhile Bones Crawford, with 4 rings and 3 MVP awards, sits outside at 7,332. Freeze a retired player's number the day he retires, or admit the Hall is a stock ticker.

takes.headline: Ryland Maxwell, Not Calvin Wingo II, Was the Offensive Player of the Year
takes.dek: Maxwell ran for 2,839 yards and took Super Bowl MVP. Wingo's yardage fell by 806 and he took the trophy.
body: Calvin Wingo II caught 98 passes for 1,764 yards and 22 touchdowns in Y92, a fine season and a clear step down from 2,570 yards and 30 touchdowns in Y91. He won Offensive Player of the Year for the lesser of the two.

Ryland Maxwell, in the same Eagles backfield Wingo shared a huddle with, ran for 2,839 yards and 32 touchdowns, caught 11 more scores and then took Super Bowl MVP. That is 142 rushing yards a game, at a position where the man who now holds the career record averages 75.2. Wingo was the second-best player in his own huddle. The award arrived a year late, for the wrong season.

takes.headline: The Y92 Eagles Were the Best Team of the Philadelphia Era, and the Margin Says So
takes.dek: The same 15-2 record as Y91, but more points, fewer allowed, less luck and a winning streak that ran through the Super Bowl.
body: The record was the same 15-2 as Y91. Nothing else was. Philadelphia scored 652 points and allowed 373, a differential of 279, up from 222 a year earlier and the best of the five Eagles seasons under Dorren Skura. Its expected wins, 13.4, were the highest of the stint, and its luck figure fell to 1.6 from 2.3, so less of this was fortune.

Then the finish: every game won from Week 6 through Super Bowl CLI, 12 in the regular season and 3 in the playoffs. The Y91 champions needed some breaks. This team needed none. It was Skura's second straight title, and it may be his most complete.

takes.headline: Indianapolis Had the MVP and the Defensive Player of the Year. Philadelphia Had the Team.
takes.dek: Korey Friend and Dwayne Skura swept the big individual awards, and the Colts still lost the Super Bowl by nine.
body: Korey Friend threw for 4,724 yards, 49 touchdowns and 4 interceptions and won MVP. Dwayne Skura won Defensive Player of the Year. Amik Barnes took the defensive rookie award. The Colts opened the year by beating the Ravens 69-12, the biggest margin in the league's game records.
And they went 11-6, with 10.7 expected wins, and lost Super Bowl CLI 30-21. Awards measure individuals. Seasons measure rosters, and Philadelphia's was deeper at every level that mattered.

Y93.reason: Hot Takes for the completed Y93 season
Y93.intro: Y93 gave Philadelphia a perfect season and Ryland Maxwell the rushing record. Perfection hides things, and records flatter. The arguments below are ours to defend; every figure comes straight from the league data.

takes.headline: Perfect Is Not the Same as Dominant: The 17-0 Eagles Were the League's Luckiest Club
takes.dek: Philadelphia's points say 13.3 wins. The schedule was soft and every close game broke its way.
body: Nobody gets to take 17-0 away from Philadelphia, and nobody should pretend the record tells the whole story either. By points scored and allowed, the Eagles played like a 13.3-win team. They won 3.7 games more than that, the biggest gap between expectation and result of any club in the league. They went 4-0 in one-score games. Their schedule rated 0.455; only the Raiders and Panthers drew softer slates.

Here is the uncomfortable part. The Y92 Eagles, the team that lost twice, outscored opponents by 279. This one managed 259. The perfect team was not the best team Dorren Skura has had in Philadelphia. It was the one the bounces loved, and the next one will not get all of them.

takes.headline: Bones Crawford Is Already a Better Quarterback Than Ty Lock Ever Was
takes.dek: Four MVPs in 113 games against two in 295. The argument is over.
body: Ty Lock has the reputation, the ratings and the longer career. Bones Crawford has everything else. The Doctor won his 4th MVP in Y93 after throwing 64 touchdown passes and 4,936 yards in 20 games. Lock, also in 20 games, threw 26 touchdowns for the Giants.

This is not one season. Crawford has averaged 3.31 touchdown passes a game across 113 career games. Lock has averaged 1.95 across 295, and has 2 MVPs to show for it. Crawford completed 281 of his 317 attempts this year. Longevity is a virtue, and Lock has it. Greatness is a different thing, and Crawford has more of it already.

takes.headline: Ty Lock's Card Rose 30% in a Down Season. The Market Is Paying for a Name.
takes.dek: His touchdowns fell from 32 to 26 and his price jumped to 4,458. A rookie with 39 sells for 16.
body: Ty Lock threw 26 touchdown passes in Y93, down from 32 a year earlier, and his card went up 30% anyway, to 4,458. That is more than double Bones Crawford's 2,198, and Crawford just threw 64. The game still rates Lock's skill a perfect 10, and the market is pricing that rating, not the production.

Meanwhile Alshon Lazard threw 39 touchdowns with 4 interceptions as a rookie in Cincinnati, and his card sits at 16. Lock has earned his place in the league's history. Paying a premium for what he did in Y93 is buying a memory. The smart money sells the name and buys the rookie.

takes.headline: Josh Brooks Threw 603 Passes Without an Interception at 38, and the League Barely Noticed
takes.dek: The cleanest season in the league belonged to a quarterback with 558 career touchdowns and no rings.
body: Bones Crawford's 64 touchdowns will get the headlines, and fine. But the most remarkable quarterback season of Y93 happened in Washington. Josh Brooks, 38 years old, threw 603 passes and not one of them was intercepted. He added 43 touchdowns and 4,061 yards in 19 games.

Brooks now has 558 career touchdown passes and 0 rings. He has spent the last six seasons in the same division as Skura's Eagles, and a 10-7 Commanders club finished third in its own division behind the Eagles and Giants. The league hands out rings to teams. If it handed out a trophy for quarterbacking without mistakes, Brooks would have won it this year by a mile.

takes.headline: Niles Canaday Scored 40 Touchdowns and Fumbled 21 Times. That Is Not a Star.
takes.dek: The Giants back outscored Ryland Maxwell on the ground and fumbled seven times as often.
body: Niles Canaday ran for 1,898 yards and 40 touchdowns in Y93, 14 more rushing scores than Ryland Maxwell. Somebody will call him the next great back. Look closer. Canaday fumbled 21 times on 202 carries. Maxwell fumbled 3 times on 225.

The game is not fooled either. It rates Canaday's skill at 1, with a ceiling of 3. Touchdowns say as much about where a back gets the ball as about the back. A back who coughs it up that often is a liability wearing a highlight reel, and the first defense that takes his carries away will expose it.

takes.headline: The Best Defender in Y93 Played for the 3-14 Saints, and His Card Costs 614
takes.dek: Trequan Roberts made 241 tackles in 17 games. The Defensive Player of the Year made 225 in 19.
body: DQ Watts won Defensive Player of the Year for Houston, and the award formula, which leans hard on interceptions, explains why: Watts picked off 5 passes to Trequan Roberts' 1. That is the whole case. Roberts made 241 tackles in 17 games, 14.2 a game. Watts made 225 in 19, 11.8 a game.

Roberts did it for a Saints team that went 3-14, and the market treats him accordingly at 614. Odell Hainsey's card sells for 7,788 after a season of 183 tackles in 17 games. One of these defenders carried a collapsing team every week. The other carries a reputation. Only one of them is priced like a star.

takes.headline: Keenan Viennes Is the Offensive Player of the Year and His Card Still Costs 49
takes.dek: He out-gained and out-scored Calvin Wingo II, whose card sells for 667. The market is a season behind.
body: Keenan Viennes caught 107 passes for 2,007 yards and 29 touchdowns and won Offensive Player of the Year. His own teammate Calvin Wingo II caught 104 for 1,976 and 19. Viennes beat him in every column that matters. Wingo's card is 667. Viennes' card is 49.

The gap is a ratings story. The market reads an overall of 73 for Viennes against 86 for Wingo, and Viennes has only 40 career games behind him. The game itself rates his speed and skill at 10 apiece, the top of the scale. Buy him now. In two seasons nobody will believe he was ever this cheap.

takes.headline: Alshon Lazard Is Already a Top Five Quarterback, and He Is Nowhere Near His Ceiling
takes.dek: Only three passers threw more touchdowns than the Rookie of the Year. The game says he has room to grow.
body: Alshon Lazard threw 39 touchdown passes and 4 interceptions in 18 games for a Bengals club that went 14-3, and he won Rookie of the Year. Only Bones Crawford, Tim Sweeney and Josh Brooks threw more touchdowns. Juju Ngakoue matched him at 39, and Ngakoue is 35. Lazard is 21.

The ratings make the case stronger. The game puts Lazard's skill at 5 today with a ceiling of 9. He is producing like a veteran on a rating with years of growth left in it. Cincinnati has its quarterback for the next decade, and the rest of the conference should be worried.

takes.headline: Ryland Maxwell Took the Career Rushing Record in the Season His Decline Began
takes.dek: He ran for 694 fewer yards than in Y92. He will finish third on the all-time Career Legacy list, not first.
body: Ryland Maxwell owns the career rushing record at 25,701 yards and won his 5th Super Bowl MVP. Celebrate it. Then look at the line. Mad Max ran for 2,145 yards in 20 games, 694 fewer than his record 2,839 in Y92. That is 107 yards a game, down from 142. His rushing touchdowns fell from 32 to 26.

He is 33. His Career Legacy of 11,965 ranks third all time, 590 behind God Johnson and 1,426 behind Sherman Brandson. He gained 964 this season. One more year like this catches Johnson. Brandson is out of reach, and the greatest-ever debate ends with a running back in third place.

takes.headline: The Raiders' 14-3 Was the Emptiest Record in Football
takes.dek: Las Vegas played the softest schedule in the league and still won about three games more than its points earned.
body: The Raiders and Bengals both finished 14-3, and only one of them earned it. Cincinnati's opponents rated 0.502, an average slate. Las Vegas drew a 0.427 schedule, the softest of all 32 clubs. By points scored and allowed the Raiders were an 11.2-win team, and they beat that by 2.8 games, a margin only the Eagles topped.

Houston went 13-4 and outscored opponents by 198, far more than the Raiders' 145. That is the AFC's best team by the numbers. When the Raiders meet a schedule with teeth, the record will look like what it was: good, lucky and soft.

takes.headline: Pittsburgh Reached the Super Bowl Without Winning Its Own Division
takes.dek: The Steelers finished behind Cincinnati, lost to a 4-13 Titans team and ranked No. 7 in power.
body: The Steelers went 11-6, finished second in the AFC North behind the Bengals, and lost 31-30 at home to a Titans team that won 4 games all year. They outscored opponents by 38 across the regular season. The power table ranked them No. 7, behind four AFC clubs.

Then they won when it counted, and credit to them for that. But Super Bowl CLII was never really a contest of equals. Philadelphia won 30-17 against a club whose points said 9.3 wins. The AFC sent the team that got hot, not its best one.
